accroche.texte: improve-codebase-architecture spots the modules to deepen for more testable code
passages: Surface architectural friction and propose deepening opportunities: refactors that turn shallow modules into deep ones.
The aim is testability and AI-navigability.

description.texte: Matt Pocock's skill starts from the files that recur most in commit history and looks there for shallow modules, those whose interface is almost as complex as the implementation. It suggests deepening them: more behavior behind a simple interface, code that is easier to test and to navigate for AI.
passages: walk back a good stretch of the commit history (git log --oneline) to find the codebase's hot spots, the files and areas that keep coming up
Where are modules shallow, with an interface nearly as complex as the implementation?
The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface.
The aim is testability and AI-navigability.

interet.texte: The suggestions arrive in an HTML report: for each one, the problem, the solution, a before/after diagram and a recommendation level. You pick one, and the agent digs into it with you before proposing any interface. Decisions already recorded in your ADRs are not called into question.
passages: present them as a visual HTML report
Files: which files/modules are involved Problem: why the current architecture is causing friction Solution: plain English description of what would change
Before / After diagram: side-by-side, custom-drawn, illustrating the shallowness and the deepening
Recommendation strength: one of Strong, Worth exploring, Speculative, rendered as a badge
Do NOT propose interfaces yet.
Once the user picks a candidate, call the Skill tool with "grilling" to walk the decision tree with them
ADRs in docs/adr/ record decisions this command should not re-litigate.

exemple_usage.texte: The author recommends running it every few days. On old code, it finds real leads without untangling everything for you.

termes_proches.raison: Mot anglais courant pour la refactorisation, usage central du skill.
La refactorisation vise un code devenu dur à faire évoluer, ce qu'on nomme souvent dette technique.
La refactorisation proposée transforme des modules superficiels en modules profonds.
Le skill cherche les modules fortement couplés qui débordent les uns sur les autres, comme pistes de refactorisation.
Le dépôt présente ce skill dans sa section « We Built A Ball Of Mud » : un code enchevêtré, où il cherche des pistes de refactorisation.
Nom courant d'un code enchevêtré : le skill y cherche des pistes de refactorisation, sans le démêler à votre place.
Le skill entretient le vocabulaire du domaine (GLOSSARY.md), notion issue du domain-driven design.
Le skill lit et met à jour le glossaire du projet, sans être un outil de glossaire.
